findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (likely milliseconds)
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors and replay events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from the nodestore event payload (`data.get("timestamp")`, line 115), which is epoch seconds. Replay recording events are rrweb events, whose timestamps are epoch milliseconds; the parser casts `payload["timestamp"]` to int and the replay code elsewhere treats them as ms. If so, every error is `<` the first replay event, so all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. Seer then gets a wrong timeline with no error. The tests use `now.timestamp()` for both the error and the recording event (test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py ~149-188), so they would not catch a unit mismatch. Normalize the units (e.g. error ts * 1000, or compare both in seconds) and add a test with realistic ms replay timestamps. I did not find a conversion in `as_log_message`/`event_parser.py`; please confirm the unit of the stored recording timestamps.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) can pair IDs with the wrong events
findings.body: `nodestore.get_multi` returns a dict that is deduplicated, omits missing nodes, and puts uncached ids before cached ones (nodestore/base.py:184-205). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` therefore misaligns whenever an id is duplicated, a node is missing, or the result mixes cached and uncached entries. The `id` field of `ErrorEvent` can then belong to a different event than its title/message/timestamp. The id is not used in the log message today, so the visible effect is nil, but it is a latent bug. Key the lookup by node id: `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled
findings.body: `query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` (lines 70-84) run before the `enable_error_context=false` check at 87-92. When the caller disables error context, the ClickHouse aggregation query is still executed and its result is unused. Move the flag check ahead of the query and only query for `error_ids` when error fetching is enabled.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity is not enforced when both are absent or when age is 0
findings.body: Field-level `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` only run when that field is present, and both fields are `required=False`. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore validates, although the comments say one of the two specs must be followed. The checks also use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` (valid per the spec: report generated just now) together with `timestamp` passes the 'mutually exclusive' check. Use a `validate()` method that checks `"age" in data` / `"timestamp" in data` and requires exactly one. The docstrings ('Validate that age is absent...') also describe the opposite of what each check does.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a Snuba query plus a DB query for every issue in the PR comment
findings.body: `issue.get_recommended_event()` runs a Snuba query (models/group.py:870-890) and `get_environment()` then does `Environment.objects.get` (eventstore/models.py:176-185), once per issue inside the list comprehension in both the GitHub and GitLab `get_comment_body`. This adds N sequential Snuba round trips to the PR comment task, with no timeout of its own beyond the broad `except Exception`. Consider batching, or reading the environment from the group's event tags already fetched. Also note failures are logged at `info`, so a persistent Snuba failure would be invisible.

findings.title: Flagged branch renders an empty table and ignores the query results
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` receives `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`, so the widget shows no data and drops `tableResults`, loading state, and title. I found no registration of this flag under src/sentry, so organizations cannot have it today, but anyone enabling it would see all dashboard table widgets blank. Either wire in `result.data`/`result.meta` or leave this out of the PR until the flag is registered.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applies while a search query is typed
findings.body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` unchanged at lines 61-63 when `searchQuery` is empty. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check at line 67 sits after that early return, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown by default and are only hidden once the user types something. `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` is the only list passed to `AttributesTree` (line 139), so nothing else hides them. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name))`.

findings.title: Flex migration drops align-items and gap that the old Container/FlexBox had
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` was `display:flex; align-items:center; gap: space(1)`, and `Container` extended it with `justify-content: space-between`. The loaded state at line 93 is now `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">`, which loses both `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}`. The tabs and `TraceContextVitals` are no longer vertically centred and have no gap between them. In `Placeholder`, the second inner `<Flex>` (line 27) also lost `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}`, so the three 100px placeholders now touch each other. Add `align="center" gap={space(1)}` to both.

findings.title: Rewrite to raw useQuery drops retry:false and staleTime, so errors keep isLoading true for several seconds
findings.body: The old `useApiQuery` call set `retry: false`. The new `useQuery` (lines 50-54) sets only `enabled`, `queryKey` and `queryFn`. `DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG` (static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26) does not override `retry`, so react-query's default of 3 retries with backoff applies. `isLoading` is now `isFetching`, so when `/trace-items/attributes/` fails, the search builder and column editors show a loading state for the whole retry window. Restore `retry: false`. Also decide on `staleTime` explicitly, since the old code set `staleTime: 0`. The queryKey also has no org slug, though `getTraceItemAttributeKeys` uses `organization.slug`; consider adding it.

findings.title: New SummaryListContainer grid item has no overflow/min-height, so the list may stop scrolling inside its row
findings.body: Previously the `list` grid item was the `FluidHeight` Container, which has `overflow: hidden` and `height: 100%`, so it was clamped to the `1fr` row. The grid item is now `SummaryListContainer` (lines 125-129), a plain flex column with neither `overflow: hidden` nor `min-height: 0`. A grid item with `overflow: visible` has an automatic minimum height, so a tall `FeedbackList` could stretch the row and be clipped by `LayoutGrid`'s `overflow: hidden` instead of scrolling inside its own container. I did not run it. Add `overflow: hidden; min-height: 0` to `SummaryListContainer` and check list scrolling with the summary shown.

findings.title: Flex replacement of FlexBox drops height: 100%
findings.body: The old `FlexBox` was `flex-grow:1; flex-direction:column; height:100%`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` renders `flex: 1` (basis 0%) and no height. If the parent does not give a definite flex height, the waterfall container may size differently. Confirm the parent's layout, or keep an explicit height.

findings.title: Typo and missing space in story copy
findings.body: Line 27 says "the the most basic example". Line 28 puts `tableData` straight after "requires" with no space, and lines 57-58 have the same problem with "type" and `TabularData`. JSX collapses the newline, so the text renders as "requirestableData" and "typeTabularData". Add `{' '}` after those words.

findings.title: Flex.Item grow={1} is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`
findings.body: The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With `auto` basis the description column starts from its max-content width. The sibling `Metadata` (line 265) has `margin-left: 4 / margin-right: 100px` and also an auto basis, so when the description text is long the shrink is shared proportionally and `Metadata` can be squeezed. With the old `0%` basis the description only took the leftover space. `Flex.Item` accepts `flex={1}`, which renders `flex: 1` and keeps the old layout exactly.

findings.title: Tests no longer cover the request-body logging or the non-list payload branch
findings.body: The `logger.info("browser_report_received", ...)` assertions were removed from `test_basic` and the multi-report test, but the endpoint still logs the raw body (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:93), so that behavior is now untested. The non-list branch (lines 99-104, a bare 422 with no body) also has no test. The new validation tests only cover the per-report serializer path. A test that posts a dict instead of a list and expects 422 would cover it.

findings.title: No test for a PUT that omits `owner`
findings.body: `BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update` only touches the owner when `"owner" in validated_data` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:67). The three new tests cover set-to-user, switch-to-team and clear (`None`). None covers an update that leaves `owner` out, which must keep the existing owner. A regression such as treating a missing key like `None` would clear owners on every unrelated edit, and no test would catch it. Consider adding a case: set an owner, PUT `self.valid_data` without `owner`, and assert the owner is unchanged.

findings.title: Two new tests duplicate ~60 lines of setup
findings.body: `test_get_with_error` and `test_get_with_error_context_disabled` repeat the same code: storing the event, `store_replays`, building the recording segment and the feature block. Only the query param and the final assertions differ. A helper such as `_setup_replay_with_error()` or a `parametrize` over `enable_error_context` would cut the repetition and make the intended difference clear.

contracts.action: Replay summarize endpoint fetches error events from nodestore and merges them into the Seer log
contracts.equivalent_path: nodestore.backend.get_multi usage elsewhere and replay details endpoint's query_replay_instance
contracts.before_after: Before: only recording-segment breadcrumbs were sent to Seer. After: error ids come from a Snuba replay query, event bodies from nodestore, then errors are merged by timestamp into the log.
contracts.visible_effect: AI replay summary now mentions errors, if timestamps are ordered correctly.
contracts.failure_mode: Nodestore failure is caught, reported via sentry_sdk and returns [] (summary silently lacks errors). Snuba failure in query_replay_instance is not caught and fails the request. Unit mismatch can mis-order errors silently.

contracts.action: PR comment body now fetches a recommended event per issue to show environment
contracts.before_after: Before: body built from group fields only. After: one Snuba query and one Environment DB query per issue.
contracts.visible_effect: Bullet text now includes ' in `env`' and truncated titles.
contracts.failure_mode: Any exception is swallowed and logged at info; comment is posted without environment.

contracts.action: Detector validator accepts an owner field and writes owner_user_id/owner_team_id
contracts.equivalent_path: ActorField use in other validators; detector index/details endpoints supply the 'organization' context it needs
contracts.before_after: Before: owner ignored. After: owner validated via parse_and_validate_actor with the org id and stored on create/update; None clears it.
contracts.visible_effect: Detector owner can be set through the API.
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid actor raises a validation error (400).

contracts.action: Visualize reduced to a single yAxis (constructor, replace, toJSON, fromJSON now returns Visualize[]); the URL round-trip goes through BaseVisualize
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously a Visualize held yAxes[] and fromJSON returned one Visualize. getVisualizesFromLocation and getAggregateFieldsFromLocation already split each BaseVisualize into one Visualize per yAxis.
contracts.before_after: Write path: updateLocationWithAggregateFields now flatMaps BaseVisualize into one JSON-stringified entry per yAxis (aggregateFields.tsx:114-120). Read path splits the same way (aggregateFields.tsx:80-91). Writable page params are typed as BaseVisualize only, and the column editor now calls toJSON before onColumnsChange (aggregateColumnEditorModal.tsx:67). A Visualize instance therefore never reaches JSON.stringify. isBaseVisualize requires yAxes[], so a Visualize instance would not match it.
contracts.visible_effect: Toolbar shows one dropdown per visualize, delete uses toSpliced, and charts and analytics use [visualize.yAxis]. Multi-yAxis URLs are split into separate charts as before.
contracts.failure_mode: A BaseVisualize with an empty yAxes array would yield no entries when written to the URL. parseBaseVisualize rejects empty yAxes on read (visualizes.tsx:129).

contracts.action: useTraceItemAttributeKeys now wraps useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys in react-query useQuery and no longer sends `environment`
contracts.equivalent_path: The old useApiQuery call with retry:false, staleTime:0, refetchOnWindowFocus:false and an environment query param.
contracts.before_after: Before: errors surfaced immediately with no retry. After: react-query default retry (3) applies, because the app defaults override only refetchOnReconnect and refetchOnWindowFocus. `environment` is dropped from the request.
contracts.visible_effect: The only consumer is TraceItemAttributeProvider. `attributes` may now be undefined, but the context spreads them, which is safe. isLoading is isFetching, so retries keep the loading state on.
contracts.failure_mode: On endpoint failure, loading state persists through the retries and the error is a plain Error rather than a RequestError.

contracts.action: New TableWidgetVisualization renders GridEditable with default head/body cell renderers
contracts.equivalent_path: Other GridEditable consumers in dashboards that render with getFieldRenderer (not compared in depth).
contracts.before_after: Custom renderers run first; a falsy return falls back to getFieldRenderer. Without tableData.meta, the raw value is returned (defaultTableCellRenderers.tsx:70-81).
contracts.visible_effect: New component with no production caller in this part; only the story uses it.
contracts.failure_mode: `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` throws if `meta` or `fields` is missing. tableData is a required prop typed as TabularData, so this relies on the type.

contracts.action: Replay AI summary tab resolves the project from replayRecord.project_id instead of the `project` URL query param, and shows a new 'Project not found' error
contracts.equivalent_path: useProjectFromId callers such as static/app/components/feedback/useFetchFeedbackData.tsx:47, which also pass the record's own project id
contracts.before_after: Before: project id came from `?project=` via useLocationQuery, so the summary request URL depended on the page URL. After: it comes from the replay record, which is always the record's project. The error branch (line 90) runs after the useApiQuery hook, so hook order is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: The summary loads whenever the record is loaded and its project is in the projects store. If the project is not in the store, the user sees the error alert, not an endless spinner.
contracts.failure_mode: If the store lacks the project, the query stays disabled and the new alert shows. When replayRecord is undefined, project_id is undefined, so the branch is skipped and the disabled query shows the spinner.

contracts.action: Browser reporting collector tests rewritten around serializer validation (422 with details)
contracts.equivalent_path: BrowserReportSerializer plus the post() handler in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py
contracts.before_after: Expected errors match the serializer: the required-field, choice, URL, min_value and DictField messages are DRF defaults. Field-level min_value runs before validate_timestamp, so timestamp=-1 yields only the min_value message. age plus timestamp triggers both cross-field validators, so both keys appear.
contracts.failure_mode: The default test format is JSON (TEST_REQUEST_DEFAULT_FORMAT), so posting a list without content_type works.

contracts.action: PR comment tests updated to the new `* ‼️ [**title**](url) in `env`` format
contracts.equivalent_path: get_comment_body in github/integration.py and gitlab/integration.py via get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info in commit_context.py
contracts.before_after: Each item is `* ‼️ [**title**](url){env}\n`, items are joined with '\n', and the template adds its own trailing newlines. That produces the blank lines and the three newlines before `<sub>` that the GitHub tests expect, and the single trailing newline in the GitLab tests. Environment text appears only when the recommended event has an environment.
contracts.failure_mode: Titles over 50 characters are truncated by the production code, but the test titles are short, so the raw titles match.

contracts.action: Visualize API tests moved to a single `yAxis` string, with fromJSON returning an array and toJSON producing `{yAxes: [...]}`
contracts.before_after: The class takes `yAxis: string`, replace() takes `yAxis`, fromJSON returns `Visualize[]`, and toJSON emits `yAxes: [yAxis]`. The spec assertions and the modal's `onColumnsChange` expectations (`{yAxes: [...]}` from col.toJSON()) match.

contracts.action: Replay bulk delete test now uses max_segment_id None
contracts.before_after: MatchedRow allows `int | None` and `_make_recording_filenames` returns [] for None. The test mocks fetch and delete, so the None path is only passed through, not exercised.

contracts.action: New replay-summary tests store an error event and replay row, then call the endpoint with and without `enable_error_context=false`
contracts.equivalent_path: ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get reads error_ids from the Snuba replay row, calls fetch_error_details (nodestore get_multi), and merges the errors into the breadcrumb log by timestamp.
contracts.before_after: The endpoint (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:84-101) skips error fetching when `enable_error_context` is `false`. Otherwise it fetches the errors and passes them to analyze_recording_segments. The tests mock make_seer_request and read the JSON payload it received. The enabled test asserts the title and message appear in `logs`. The disabled test asserts they do not.
contracts.visible_effect: Test-only. Seer receives error lines only when error context is enabled.
contracts.failure_mode: If the Snuba insert fails, store_replays asserts status 200. If the nodestore fetch fails, fetch_error_details swallows the exception and returns [], so the enabled test would fail on its assertion and not pass silently.

contracts.action: Detector create/update tests post `owner` as a user or team actor identifier, `None`, or an invalid value
contracts.equivalent_path: BaseDetectorTypeValidator.owner is an ActorField, which uses parse_and_validate_actor. `create` and `update` map the actor to owner_user_id or owner_team_id.
contracts.before_after: ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True) passes `None` through, so update clears both owner columns. An unparseable identifier or an actor outside the organization raises a ValidationError, which returns a 400 keyed on `owner`. The detector serializer returns `owner` as `actor.identifier`. The tests assert each of these behaviours.
contracts.visible_effect: API responses include `owner` as `user:<id>` or `team:<id>`, or null.
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid actors return a 400 with an `owner` key. Nothing is silent.

contracts.action: Delayed-workflow tests pass a precomputed `dcg_to_slow_conditions` into get_condition_query_groups and get_groups_to_fire
contracts.equivalent_path: The production caller computes `get_slow_conditions_for_groups(list(event_data.dcg_ids))` once and passes the result to both functions.
contracts.before_after: The tests build the same mapping after creating all conditions, using the same ids as the event data. test_multiple_dcgs_per_group reuses the mapping with an extended event_data that has the same DCG set, so every dcg.id lookup is present.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing key would raise KeyError in the code under test. All DCGs looked up are covered.

contracts.action: New logs top-events test calls /events-stats/ with dataset=ourlogs and topEvents=5
contracts.equivalent_path: The spans top-events tests in the same file use the same RPC path (`use_rpc = dataset in {spans_rpc, ourlogs}`).
contracts.before_after: Six distinct bodies are stored with 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 rows. The top 5 plus "Other" (10) are expected. There are no ties, so the ordering is deterministic. The old class name `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEvents` has no other references, so the rename to `...Spans` is safe.
contracts.failure_mode: Only the first time bucket is asserted. All rows fall within the first hour, so this is sufficient.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** I found one likely wrong-result bug and five smaller points in this part. The most important is in the replay breadcrumbs endpoint: error timestamps look to be in seconds and replay events in milliseconds, so errors would all land at the start of the Seer log. I read the code only and ran nothing.

- **Replay breadcrumbs (`project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`):**
  - The unit mismatch above is a "fix" with medium confidence, because I could not find a ms/s conversion for recording timestamps. The tests use `now.timestamp()` for both sides, so they would not catch it.
  - `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can pair ids with the wrong events when ids repeat or nodes are missing. The id is not used in the log message today.
  - The Snuba replay query still runs when `enable_error_context=false`.
- **Browser reporting collector:** a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation. The exclusivity check uses truthiness, so `age: 0` alongside `timestamp` also passes.
- **PR comment environment (`commit_context.py`):** `get_environment_info` makes one Snuba query and one DB query per issue.
- **Dashboard chart (`chart.tsx`):** the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders an empty table and ignores the query results. I found no registration of that flag under `src/sentry`, so nobody can hit it today.

The rest of the part looked fine. This includes the migration stubs (0921 exists), the delayed-workflow refactor (`dcg_ids` equals the old `dcg_to_groups` keys), the detector `owner` field, the new devservices consumers and the removed grouping experiment.

**Batch 2 of 4.** I found two defects to fix in this part and three smaller points for the author to weigh. I only read the code; nothing was built or run.

- **Hidden attributes:** the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter in `attributes.tsx` runs after the empty-search early return. `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` therefore still show by default and are only hidden once the user types a search.
- **Trace header layout:** the `Flex` migration in `traceTabsAndVitals.tsx` dropped `align-items: center` and `gap` from the old `Container` and `FlexBox`. The tabs and vitals lose their vertical centring, and the loading placeholders now touch each other.
- **Attribute-keys hook:** `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` lost `retry: false`, so a failing request stays in the loading state through react-query's default retries.
- **Feedback list and trace waterfall:** the new `SummaryListContainer` may let the feedback list stretch its grid row instead of scrolling, and `traceWaterfall.tsx` lost `height: 100%`. I could not confirm either without running it.
- **Story typos:** the table story has a "the the" typo and missing spaces around `<code>` in its copy.

The single-`yAxis` `Visualize` refactor holds up: I traced URL writes and reads, and no `Visualize` instance reaches `JSON.stringify`. I could not verify the `sampleHTTPRequestTableData` fixture or the spec files, which are in other parts.

**Batch 3 of 4.** Part 3 is mostly mechanical styled-div to `Flex` swaps plus test updates. The tests match the code at head: Visualize API, `useGetTraceItemAttributeValues`, browser-reporting validation, PR comment format, autofix default "off", and the TableWidget spec. One consider-level finding: in integrationLayout.tsx, `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1` because the flex-basis changes from 0% to auto. A second consider-level finding: the browser-reporting tests dropped the request-body logging assertion and never test the non-list payload branch.

**Batch 4 of 4.** I found nothing that blocks this part. All five test files are consistent with the code under test. Two minor suggestions: add a detector test for a PUT that omits `owner`, and deduplicate the two new replay-summary tests. I only read the code and ran nothing.
